issuenote: Three Burundi army officers have been arrested for suspected involvement in a failed bid to assassinate a top advisor to the president.

issuenote: A laptop bomb went off at an airport security checkpoint, wounding 6 people, two of them policemen.
notes: Al-Shabab wants to overthrow Somalia's weak U.N.-backed government and govern Somalia under a harsh interpretation of Islamic law.  Beledweyne is located in the Hiiraan region.

issuenote: US Military advisors and Somali special forces conducted a night raid targeting the anti-government Al-Shabaab
notes: Hoping to capture a high-profile target, Somali forces hopped off helicopters a couple of miles from an al-Shabab-controlled town, slipped through the dark and got into a fierce firefight that reportedly killed more than 10 Islamic extremists

issuenote: A car bomb detonated outside a tea shop near the police academy in the capital.
notes: Three police officers and one civilian were killed as they drank tea.

issuenote: Islamist extremists tried to take control of two small villages near the port of Eyl.  They engaged government forces and were defeated.
notes: Eyl is a pirating hotspot.  65 militants were killed and 31 taken prisoner (most of them were children).  The anti-government extremists were defeated by Puntland region's security forces, who killed 11 of the attackers.

issuenote: Islamist extremists tried to take control of two small villages near the port of Eyl.  They engaged government forces and were defeated.
notes: Eyl is a pirating hotspot.  65 militants were killed and 31 taken prisoner (most of them were children).  The anti-government extremists were defeated by Puntland region's security forces, who killed 11 of the attackers.

issuenote: Kenyan Defense Forces thwarted a Shebab attack on a base is operated by the Somali National Army (SNA) and AMISOM.
notes: The KDF operates in support of the government.  19 militants were killed, a technical vehicle was destroyed, 10 AK 47s and 3 rocket propelled grenades were seized.  Afmadhow is located in the Lower Juba area (Southern Somalia)

issuenote: Shebab militants tried to ambush the town of Afmadhow, where Kenyan Defense Forces engaged the attackers.
notes: 21 militants and 2 Kenyan soldiers were killed.  The KDF operates in support of the government.

issuenote: Kenyan Defense Force under AMISOM authority conducted an operation which killed 13 militants and seized some AK47s and RPGs.
notes: Shebab fighters have targeted AMISOM in Somalia because, in the absence of a functioning national army, the 22,000-strong force is the only protector of the internationally-backed government that the jihadists are committed to overthrowing

issuenote: Kenyan Defense Force under AMISOM authority conducted an operation which killed 13 militants and seized some AK47s and RPGs.
notes: Shebab fighters have targeted AMISOM in Somalia because, in the absence of a functioning national army, the 22,000-strong force is the only protector of the internationally-backed government that the jihadists are committed to overthrowing

issuenote: Hundreds of Shebab militants stormed a Somali military base, looted depots, set fire to the camp, and claimed to have killed 73 government soldiers.
notes: The base is located 40 kilometers outside of the capital.  The government claims to have fought off the attack.

issuenote: A drive-by shooting killed six people and wounded six more.
notes: Two Turkish hospital workers, their driver, and their security guard were all killed.  Turkey is a major donor to Somalia and the event prompted the Somali President to condemn the event and express unity with Turkish people.

issuenote: A suicide attack on a hotel resulted in the death of the head of the finances for Puntland along with five of his bodyguards.
notes: Galkayo is about 650 kilometers (400 miles) northeast of the capital Mogadishu between the two districts of Puntland and Galmudug.  In addition to the deaths 10 people were wounded.

issuenote: The US military and Somali officials conducted a drone attack that killed a major Al-Shebab leader, Hassan Ali Dhoore.
notes: Dhoore was an intelligence chief for Al-Shebab who helped facilitate a deadly Christmas Day 2014 attack at Mogadishu International Airport and a March 2015 attack at the Maka al-Mukarramah Hotel.

issuenote: A remote detonated car bomb exploded outside of a restaurant which is frequented by Somali Security Forces.
notes: Three civilians were killed and five injured.

issuenote: A car bomb was detonated in front of shops near the headquarters of the local government during the busy lunch hour.
notes: Five civilians were killed and seven others wounded.  Two of the dead were children.  Shebab did not claim the attack but the UN mission said it "bears hallmarks" of a Shebab operation.

issuenote: A pair of drone strikes were conducted that targeted Shebab militants who were threatening US and Somali forces.
notes: The attack took place outside of the major urban area, just North of Kismayo.

issuenote: An explosive device was detonated at a busy livestock market.
notes: Afgoye is located about 20 miles south of the capital and has a population of about 80,000 people.  6 people were wounded.

issuenote: AMISOM forces accidentally killed four civilians after soldiers mistook them for Shebab fighters when they failed to stop at a roadblock.
notes: Security forces thought the car was a Vehicle Borne Improvised Explosive Device (VBIED).  Buulo Mareer is located in the Lower Shebelle region, 80 kilometers (50 miles) south of the capital Mogadishu.

issuenote: Islamic extremist used a suicide car bomb and attacked the town of Runirgod from three directions.  The attack was to recapture the town, which had been seized by government forces the day before.
notes: Runirgod is located in the Middle Shabelle region.  Al-Shabab claimed it killed 32 soldiers during the attack but their figures are often exaggerated.

issuenote: A suicide car bomber struck the entrance of Somalia's traffic police headquarters.
notes: Two police officers and two attackers were killed in the blast.  Nine others were injured.

issuenote: Somali commandos trained by US forces used two helicopters to conduct a raid, which Shebab Extremists were able to repel.
notes: Toratorow is located about 60 kilometers south of the capital.  Civilians reported hearing explosions and gunfire throughout the forty minute engagement.

issuenote: US special operations forces conducted an air strike against an illegal al-Shebab roadblock being used to extort payments from drivers.
notes: Ugandan AMISOM forces were fired upon by Shebab at a rural road in an uninhabited area and US forces responded by calling in a drone airstrike.

issuenote: Kenyan AMISOM forces found a group of Islamist Extremists positioned to conduct and ambush.
notes: The Kenyan AMISOM forces killed 21 extremists.  Tabda, where the Kenyan forces were headed, is located in the Lower Juba (Jubbada Hoose) region of Southern Somalia.

issuenote: US Military officials at the Pentagon conducted an air strike that killed Abdullahi Haji Da'ud, one of Shebab's most senior military planners.
notes: No location data was provided.  Da'ud served as a principal coordinator of previous militia attacks in Somalia, Kenya, and Uganda.

target2: Mohamed Mohamud Ali (aliases Dulyadin, Kuno, and Gamadhere)
issuenote: Somali special forces of the Jubaland conducted a raid against Al-Shabaab.
notes: Four senior commanders were killed.  The Shebab commander "Dulyadin" was targeted in the raid.  He was the suspected architect of the bloodbath in Garissa, Kenya from 2015 that killed 148 people who were mostly students sleeping in a college dormitory.

issuenote: A VBIED (vehicle-borne improvised explosive device) exploded at the Ambassador Hotel, popular with MPs and foreigners.  The explosion was followed by a firefight between Islamist extremists and security forces.
notes: Two lawmakers were among the dead.  Around 34 people were injured and the follow up attack lasted for more than twelve hours.

issuenote: Shebab fighters attacked an Ethiopian army base in a raid targeting foreign soldiers deployed as part of an African Union force in the country.
notes: Halgan is located in the central Hiran region of Somalia.  The number of deaths is widely disputed by AMISOM and Shebab officials, but conservative estimates are 30 Ethiopians and 110 militants.

issuenote: Shebab jihadists publicly executed six men they accused of spying and helping to target their commanders killed in recent air strikes.
notes: Four spies were killed in Bulofay, in the Bay region in the southwest of the country.  Two more were publicly executed in the Jubbada Dhexe region, also in the southwest

issuenote: Shebab jihadists publicly executed six men they accused of spying and helping to target their commanders killed in recent air strikes.
notes: Four spies were killed in Bulofay, in the Bay region in the southwest of the country.  Two more were publicly executed in the Jubbada Dhexe region, also in the southwest

issuenote: An attack on the Nasa-Hablod hotel began when a suicide bomber detonated an explosives-laden vehicle at the hotel entrance, ripping off its gate. Gunmen fought their way inside and began shooting randomly at hotel guests.
notes: A Somali Cabinet Minister and four attackers were counted among the 15 killed.

issuenote: A roadside bomb ripped apart a minibus carrying civilians just outside of the capital.
notes: There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the blast, but Somalia's Al-Qaeda-linked Shebab has carried out a string of similar attacks in the past.

issuenote: Mortar fire that was aimed at the regional airport landed in civilian neighborhoods.
notes: 18 people were wounded.  Shebab did not claim responsibility, but it is assumed to be the culprit because Baidoa's airport is the biggest Ethiopian base in the AMISOM mission to which they oppose.

issuenote: Shebab extremists detonated a car bomb and then entered a Somali military base on foot.  They captured the installation, seizing vehicles and weapons.
notes: The Lanta Buro military base is located in the Lower Shabelle region.  The extremists claim they killed 30 military officials.

issuenote: Two suicide car bombs attacked two different locations in the capital, one outside a UN mine clearing agency and the other at a Somali security checkpoint.
notes: Both attacks were close to an African Union facility close to the airport.  Seven of the deaths were guards and two were the bombers themselves.  Shebab claims that one of the suicide bombers was a former Somali lawmaker named Salah Badbado.

issuenote: Two suicide car bombs attacked the police Criminal Investigations Department in the capital, followed by two attackers on foot who were immediately killed by security forces.
notes: There were five victims and four dead attackers.

issuenote: Two suicide car bombs attacked a local government headquarters, the first was a truck and the second was a minibus.  A busy marketplace near the building incurred most of the casualties.
notes: Galkayo is the capital of the Mudug region, located about 440 miles northeast of the capital, Mogadishu. Shebab claimed they killed 30 people but government officials claimed 17 killed and 30 injured.

issuenote: A car refused to stop for security forces at a checkpoint outside the new Turkish embassy in the capital.  The vehicle prematurely exploded a VBIED when police forces opened fire on it.  Hours later two armed extremists attacked the nearby Benadir Beach restaurant.
notes: Six civilians and two soldiers were killed in the follow up attack.

issuenote: Shebab militants claimed an attack where a large suicide bomb was detonated outside of the presidential compound at the SYL hotel.
notes: The SYL hotel is located close to the main entrance to the Villa Somalia government complex that includes the presidential palace, ministry buildings and residences.  Shebab claimed 30 people were killed. 45 people were wounded in addition to the 15 dead claimed by the government.

issuenote: The US military and Somali officials announced the death of four Islamist extremists in an operation that included air strikes in a self-defense operation.
Heavily-armed Shebab fighters seized control of Elwak, a Somali town near the Kenyan border.
notes: Witness said the jihadists had entered the town disguised as Kenyan soldiers.

issuenote: A suicide bomber rammed an explosives-packed car into the vehicle of a top Somali General.
notes: The attack took place near Somalia's defense ministry compound.  The general was influential in the fight against the Shebab.  Five of his security guards died with him.

issuenote: Somali citizens took to the streets to protest Kenyan claims regarding disputed territory in the Indian Ocean that may have oil and gas reserves.
notes: Just two days later the UN's ICJ was expected to make a decision about whether it had jurisdiction to hear a case regarding the dispute between Somali and Kenya.  The fate of lucrative oil and gas extraction projects was at stake.

issuenote: Shebab militants attacked Somali and US forces, who killed at least four attackers in self-defense with air strikes.
notes: Shebab attacked on 26/09/2016 and an unknown number of extremists were killed by Somali forces.  The next day four extremists were killed in US defensive air strikes.

issuenote: The US conducted an air strike for a Somali-led counterterrorism operation to disrupt an al-Shabaab Improvised Explosive Device (IED) making network.  The Puntland military is accused of pointing the US airstrikes at military forces from the neighboring Galmudug state.
notes: The Galmudug government claims the US was duped into attacking it by the [semi-autonomous] Puntland government who wrongfully claimed Galmudug forces were al-Shebab.  Galkayo is a town divided between the rival states of Puntland and Galmudug.

issuenote: A car bomb blew up at the entrance of a restaurant close to the presidential palace, killing two.
notes: There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the bombing but the Islamic extremist group of al-Shabab often carries out such attacks.  Shebab is fighting to overthrow the government and implement a strict Islamic Sharia law.

issuenote: A week of violent clashes between rival forces in northern Somalia killed 11 people and forced more than 50,000 to flee because of tensions between the rival regions of Puntland and Galmudug.  In late September US airstrikes directed by Puntland Security forces killed 13 forces from Galmudug which was supposed to be targeting Shebab fighters.
notes: Galkayo (Gaalkacyo) is the capital of the north-central Mudug region of Somalia.  Galkayo lies about 700 kilometers (440 miles) northeast of Mogadishu, is not under the control of the central government, and has seen frequent clashes between rival groups and clans.

issuenote: After being targeted overnight with Shebab artillery, hundreds of Ethiopian troops pulled out of their defense positions in the El-Ali region of Somalia that they were protecting under the AMISOM joint regional military alliance.  Shebab militants proceeded to occupy the town.
notes: El-Ali is located in the Hiran region, about 70 kilometers (43 miles) from the provincial capital Beledweyne.  El-Ali was at the second town Ethiopian troops vacated in the previous weeks, after abandoning nearby Moqokori.

issuenote: Al-Shabaab attacked the city of Afgoye with a suicide bomber using a explosives-laden vehicle near a Somali police station and African Union base. Gunmen then attacked military bases.
notes: Afgoye is a town of about 80,000 people located 30 kilometers (18 miles) north of the capital, Mogadishu.  Police say two al-Shabab fighters and five Somali soldiers were killed.  Al-Shabab claims its fighters killed more than 40 soldiers during the clashes.  Somali security forces have retook the town began conducting security patrols.

issuenote: Somali pirates released 26 Asian sailors from the FV Naham 3 who were held hostage for more than four years after a ransom was paid.  The hostages were turned over to the Galmudug government.
notes: The released hostages included crew from Vietnam, Taiwan, Cambodia, Indonesia, China and the Philippines from a Taiwan-owned fishing vessel seized in March 2012.  Two crew members died of illness while in captivity.

issuenote: A Shebab suicide bomber rammed a vehicle loaded with explosives into an African Union military base ran by the Djiboutian Military in the city of Beledweyne.
notes: Al-Shebab claimed responsibility over the radio.  The African Union tweeted that a firefight with 10 extremists followed the truck bombing and said the extremists were "all killed".

issuenote: As Ethiopia was experiencing anti-government protests they withdrew forces from Somalia, giving the Shebab Islamic Militants access to the city.
notes: Tiyeglow is a small town in the southwestern Bakool region with a population of about 2,000.  The article mentions Shebab killed some elders, but did not give an exact number.

issuenote: Several dozen armed men belonging to an Islamic State-linked group on Wednesday seized control of a small port in Somalia's Puntland region.
notes: Amaq, the IS news agency, reported that Qandala, located on the Gulf of Aden opposite Yemen, had been taken by "Islamic State fighters".  Shebab doesn't operate in that area.

issuenote: Shebab militants took over the town of Haglan after hundreds of Ethiopian troops serving with the African Union's AMISOM force withdrew.
notes: Halgan is situated about 70 kilometers (40 miles) from the provincial capital Beledweyne in the central Hiran region.

issuenote: A suicide car bomber targeted an army convoy near parliament headquarters in Somalia's capital.
notes: The car bomb was detonated at the Sayidka junction of the city.  Al Shebab claimed responsibility over the radio.  The two victims were Somali soldiers.

issuenote: There was fighting over the weekend between rival Puntland and Galmudug regional forces in the divided Somali town of Galkayo which marked the collapse of a short-lived peace agreement between the two semi-autonomous Somali states.
notes: Galkayo is located 700 kilometers (440 miles) northeast of the capital.  Puntland lost 12 men and had 10 wounded.  Galmudug lost 13 and had 20 wounded.

issuenote: A car bomb was detonated at a busy marketplace in the capital.
notes: The blast occurred in the Afisiyone area in southern Mogadishu.  It is believed to have targeted a police station next to the market.  No group has yet claimed responsibility for the attack, but immediate suspicion fell on the Al-Qaeda linked Islamist Shebab group, which is locked in battle with the Somali government and regularly mounts attacks in the city.

issuenote: Fighting erupted after al-Shabab fighters who control part of the port town of Harardhere ordered nomadic villagers to pay a tax.
notes: The town has a population of more than 45,000 and is located in the Mudug region.  Six militants and four residents were reported dead after the villagers conducted an ambush.

issuenote: A suspected suicide car bomber detonated an explosives-laden vehicle at a security checkpoint near Mogadishu when soldiers stopped him for security checks.
notes: There was no information provided about the casualties in this attack.

issuenote: A suicide truck bombing occurred in the capital that Shebab claimed the target was a police station close to the port.
notes: Most of the victims were port workers and police officers.

issuenote: Two car bombs went off within a couple of hours.  A bomb hidden inside a teashop in Somalia's capital exploded.  Prior to this a driver detonated a bomb while being chased by police near the presidential palace
notes: The teashop bomb killed four soldiers and two civilians.  The other driver only killed himself.

issuenote: Troops killed a bus full of people that evaded a security checkpoint.  They turned out to be six civilians carrying vegetables to the capital.
notes: Troops have been on high alert because of recent attacks from Al-Shebab

issuenote: An al-Shebab car bomb targeting AMISOM forces exploded in a civilian home, killing a mother and her four children
notes: The bomb was intended for AMISOM security forces nearby.

issuenote: A suicide bomber detonated his vehicle at a checkpoint, killing three members of the Somalian security forces, though a second vehicle bomb was destroyed by AU peacekeepers before it could reach its target.
notes: From the context of the article, it is unclear whether the AU peacekeepers killed the drived of the second vehicle before it detonated.

issuenote: A bomb explosion at a restaurant frequented by government soldiers killed three people.
notes: AP notes that while al-Shabaab was suspected of orchestrating the attack, no one had claimed responsbility at the time the story was published.

issuenote: Militants executed a teenage boy and a man for engaging in sexual conduct, and another man for spying for the Ethiopian army.
notes: AP notes that al-Shabaab annonced the executions on January 10, though it is not clear whether they took place on this same date as well.

issuenote: A militant executed a captured Ugandan soldier after forcing him to make a video warning other AU peacekeepers not to deploy to Somalia
notes: A video of the incident was released on January 17, though it is not clear whether the execution took place on the same date. The soldier was captured by al-Shabaab in September 2015, and according to AFP, as appeared in previous al-Shabaab propaganda videos.

issuenote: Four men sexually-assaulted a 16 year-old girl.
notes: According to AP, a video of the incident was released on social media, prompting an outcry on social media. While AP released the story on January 18, it notes that the date of the incident is unknown. AP also reports that three of the alleged attackers had been arrested at the time the story was released.

issuenote: Miltants stormed a hotel frequented by government officials, killing at least 26 people and injuring 52, while suffering four casulaties as security forces recaptured the building.
notes: The fatality figure provided here is an estimate; AP reports that 26 patrons and four militants were killed in the attack, while AFP says 28 patrons were killed. Among the fatalities were two clan elders who were also staying at the hotel, according to another clan elder.

issuenote: Militants executed three men accused of collaborating with the CIA and Kenyan and Somalia government to carry out airstrikes against al-Shabaab.

issuenote: Militants attacked and overran a Kenyan army base with suicide trucks and machine guns.
notes: The fatality figure is unclear; al-Shabaab claimed to have captured the base and kiled 57 soldiers, while a KDF spokesman denied these claims and stated that 9 Kenyan soldiers and two policemen had died, while killing 70 militants. A Somalian official confrimed that the Kenayan soldiers fought back before retreating, but did not give a casaulty figure. According to AFP, "Shabaab frequently overstates the death toll from its attacks while Kenya commonly underplays its losses".

Militants clashed with peacekeepers
notes: The fatality figure is unknown; an AU statement quoted by AP said that while the AU suffered no casulaties, that expected that the militants had.

issuenote: Suspected militants fired two mortar rounds near an airport were legislators were meeting to select a new President of Somalia.
Militants attacked a hotel frequented by government officials, killing at least four guards while suffering two casualties.
notes: Although AP reported at the time that there was no immediate claim of responsibility, a subsequent AFP article about another ISIS attack stated that the group had claimed credit for this incident.

issuenote: Nine lawmakers were ejected from the regional parliament after shouting at the regional president during a debate on the opening a foreign military base in the region.
notes: The United Arab Emirates was seeking to open a naval base at Berbera for use in the conflict in Yemen; a measure which Silyano supported. The parliament approved the opening of the based by 144-2, with two abstentions.

issuenote: Militants launched a mortar attack near the presidential place during a handover ceremony for the new president, killing two children
A car bomb went off in a marketplace, killing 34 people.
notes: AP and AFP both note that while the incident bears the hallmarks of an al-Shabaab attack, no one had claimed responsbility. The fatality figure provided here is an estimate; AFP reported that there were 39 fatalities, while AP put the figure at "at least 34".

issuenote: A joint Somali-AU assault on an al-Shabaab camp killed at least 57 militants and resulted in the capture or destruction of vehicles and equipment.
notes: According to AP, there was no immediate word as to whether the AU-Somali forces suffered any casualties.

issuenote: A TV technician was wounded by a bomb planted in his car.
notes: AP notes that while al-Shabaab frequently carries out attacks in the same neighborhood of Mogadishu where this incident occurred, no one had claimed credit for the attack.

issuenote: Two suicide bombers detonated car bombs  at a military camp and the Weheliye hotel, killing at least six people and injuring 12 others.
notes: The fatality figure provided here is an estimate; police stated that at least six people had been killed at the hotel, but witnesses near the hotel said they saw between 7 and 10 bodies. In their statement claiming credit for the attack, al-Shabaab said the hotel was targeted because it is frequented by government officials.

target1: Crew of the oil tanker Aris 13
issuenote: Two dozen armed men hijacked an oil tanker to protest illegal fishing off their coasts.
notes: AFP spoke with elders in the village where the tanker was being held, who said that "the pirates had not made clear demands, but claimed to be driven by anger over illegal fishing". While the coast guard exchanged gunfire with the ship bringing supplies to the hijackers, there were no reported fatalities (though an unknown number were injured), and the ship was released after negotiations were held.

issuenote: A car bomb was detonated at a military checkpoint near the presidential palace, killing one soldier and five civilians while wounding a dozen others.
Militants were repulsed after attacking Somali army positions and shelled AU bases.
notes: The fatality figure provided here is an estimate; al-Shabaab claims to have killed 17 soldiers, while the Somali government claims that only 2 soldiers died in the attack.

issuenote: A car bomb detonated in the middle of the road near a hotel and restaurant, killing one person and wounding two others.
notes: AP notes that while al-Shabaab recently carried out an attack in the same area of Mogadishu where this incident occurred, no one had claimed credit for this incident.

issuenote: Kenyan troops raided two al-Shabaab camps.
notes: The fatality figure is an estimate; the KDF claims that 31 militants were killed, while al-Shabaab denies that the incident occurred.

issuenote: Pirates hijacked a cargo ship, taking 10 Indian crewman hostage who were later freed in two separate rescue attempts.
notes: Two crewmen were rescued on April 10; the remained were freed on April 12, when three priates were also arrested.

target1: Hanad Ali Guled, journalist with Goobjoog radio and TV station
issuenote: Six men abducted and tortured a journalist on his way to work, who was then bound and left in a field.
notes: AP notes that there was no claim of responsibility for this incident, though Guled had received death threats the day before. The location of the incident is also unclear; Guled was found in 30 km south of Mogadishu in Afgoye, though it is not clear whether we was captured in this village, or if not, how far is abduction location is from where he was released.

issuenote: A surging crowd around the site of a car bombing was dispersed by soldiers firing their weapons.
A car bomb detonated in front of a restaurant, killing at least seven people.
notes: AP notes that while al-Shabaab frequently carries out this kind of attack, no one had claimed credit for the attack. However, it did quote a police official who blamed al-Shabaab for the attack.

issuenote: A minibus struck a roadside bomb, killing at least 19 passengers, mainly women and children.
notes: AP and AFP note that while no group claimed immediate responsbility for the attack, control of this area is contested between the government and al-Shabaab, with the later commonly using roadside bombs. AFP also quoted a local police officer who blamed the attack on al-Shabaab. The number of fatalities provided here is an estimate; AP says that 20 people were killed, while AFP puts the death toll at 19.

issuenote: Three civilians were killed when at least two mortar rounds struck a residential area.
notes: AP notes that while there was no claim of responsibility for this incident, this neighborhood is near Mogadishu International Airport, which has been targeted by al-Shabaab in the past.

issuenote: Soldiers fired into the air to disperse a crowd that gathered after a suicide attack.

target1: Mohamed Ahmed Jimale, Chief of the Somali National Army, and other senior military officials
issuenote: A militant drove a minibus filled with explosives into a convoy carrying the head of the army, destroying military vehicles and a city bus and killing seven civilians and three soldiers.
notes: The fataility figure provided here is an estiamte; AFP quoted an army official who said that seven civlians and three soldiers had been killed (plus the bomber), while AP quoted a senior policy official who said that eight civilians and five soldiers (plus the bomber) were killed. Jimale, who had been sworn in as the new army chief only moments before, escaped unharmed from the attack.

target1: Abdikadir Osman, official at the education ministry
issuenote: An offical was killed when his car was blown-up with a remote-control bomb.
notes: The incident is mentioned in an article about an al-Shabaab bombing that occurred on the same day; however, it is unclear from the context of the article whether al-Shabaab claimed credit for this attack as well.

issuenote: A suicide bomber disguised as a military trainee detonated himself inside a military training camp, killing five soldiers.
notes: AP gave the fatality figure of 5 soldiers- including two officers and the camp's chief trainer- while AFP quoted a military official who only stated that "several" had been killed.

issuenote: A roadside bomb struck a convoy carrying UN officials on a supervision mission, injuring two bodyguards.
Two militants who fired mortars near the airport were pursued by and clashed with security forces, and finally detonated the minibus they were travelling in.
notes: According to AP, no casualties were reported from the blast that destoryed the minibus.

issuenote: Foreign naval forces intercepted a boat carrying nine pirates who were attempting to hijack a ship, killing two of the pirates.
Kenyan troops destroyed an al-Shabaab camp, killing 52 militants and recovering an assortment of weapons.
notes: AP notes that previous Kenyan statements about battlefield victories have been dipsuted by local residents, and that al-Shabaab had not immediately released a statement about the incident.

issuenote: Eight soldiers were killed and three injured when a military convoy struck a roadside bomb.

issuenote: Protests by ethnic Oromo over the expansion of Addis Ababa expanded to other regions of the  country and have been met with a violent response by the government.
notes: The number of participants in this incident is not mentioned. The start date given here is an estimate, as AFP states only that the protests began on the week of November 15. There is some dispute over the number of deaths associated with the suppression of these protests; Human Rights Watch initially claimed the total was at least 140 and later revised their estimate to over 400, while the official government death toll was initially 5 but later revised to 173 including 28 members of the security forces. The Ethiopia-based Human Rights Council accuses security forces of perpetrating "extrajudicial killings, tortures, beatings, illegal detentions, forced disappearances and arson attacks" during and after the protests, and provided a death toll of 173 which was adopted by the government. In addition to long-standing ethnic tensions between the Oromo and the government, Oromo farmers are concerned that this new expansion of Addis Ababa will displace them from their land. The expansion plan was abandoned by the Oromia government on January 12. However, according to HRW the crackdown on the protestors was still ongoing as of February 25. By October, international human rights groups and the UN claimed that at least 500 demonstrators had been killed in the crackdown.

According to AFP, around a dozen students participated in this incident. When the students approached the Ministry of Education, police asked them why they were there, and then fired tear gas and live bullets to disperse them. One student, Elias Arasasa, died from his wounds, while his sister was also wounded.

According to the Ethiopian government's initial reports, at least 140 civilians were killed by the raiders and 60 raiders were killed by security forces, though the civilian death toll was later revised to 208 killed and 125 children kidnapped. In addition, 2,000 livestock were also stolen. The motive for the raid is unclear; although similar, smaller-scale raids have included the kidnapping of children and theft of cattle, the Ethiopian foreign ministry spokesperson indicated that something of this magnitude was different.

A rocket attack in Zawiya killed a Filipino oil worker and wounded five other civilians.
IS fighters attacked a checkpoint outside of Misrata, killing 7 fighters from the Libya Shield Force, which is part of the Fajr Libya alliance.
An IS suicide bomber blew up a vehicle at the Saddada checkpoint east of Misrata, killing 6 people (mostly militiamen) and injuring 21.
10 soldiers were killed and 40 were wounded when government forces clashed with armed groups in Benghazi.
Loyalist fighters and Fajr militia fought for two days in Aziziya.

Gunmen opened fire on the South Korean embassy compound from a passing car, killing two guards and wounding a third person; hours later, a bomb exploded outside the Moroccan embassy but caused no casualties. IS  claimed responsibility for both attacks.
Airstrikes were carried out against the Tripoli airport.
notes: The actor responsible was not officially confirmed, but is suspected to be the Tobruk-based government.

issuenote: Loyalist forces attacked Tajoura and Tripoli in an attempt to wrest control from Fajr Libya; it was reported that 3 civilians were killed in Tripoli, and that 14 soldiers, 4 Fajr Libya fighters, and 3 civilians were killed in Tajoura.
notes: A Fajr Libya spokesman stated that 32 government soldiers were killed.

protesters in eastern Libya shut oil deliveries to a port.
notes: Exact date uncertain.

issuenote: The Libyan air force attacked a Turkish cargo vessel after it was asked several times to turn back from the coast and did not; a sailor was killed.

Shelling in several residential neighborhoods in Benghazi killed at least 27 people in the course of several days, including 10 children; no actor was identified, but a source suspected some shelling was due to the killing of an IS fighter earlier in the week.
notes: One source stated dozens had been killed in the shelling.

issuenote: IS fighters attacked the town of Harawa; armed men in the town fought back, but two of their wounded were captured and taken to the IS base in Nofaliyah, where they were beheaded.
notes: Exact date uncertain.

notes: Exact date uncertain; only month known; one source stated 245 Tunisians were captured.

IS claimed responsibility for two suicide bombings: one at a checkpoint near Harawa which killed a militia fighter, and one the next day 60km east of Misrata, which killed 1 fighter and injured 3.

IS seized the town of Harawa after a weeklong seige; IS fighters then met with local officials to negotiate access to the town and its mosques.

issuenote: Gunmen attacked Prime Minister al-Thinni's motorcade on the way to the Tobruk airport, wounding one guard; prior to the attack, armed men had protested outside the House of Representatives and attempted to storm the building, firing shots in the air and calling for the removal of al-Thinni from office.
IS took control over the Sirte airport after Fajr Libya troops withdrew from it.
IS claimed a car suicide bombing that killed 5 fighters of Fajr Libya at a checkpoint at the Dafniya entrance to Misrata.
IS attacked a militia checkpoint at near the town of Abu Grain and captured and later killed 3 Misrata militia.

issuenote: IS seized the last Fajr Libya-controlled areas of Sirte and took over the city, including a militia compound on the road to Misrata.
Government air forces targeted a Dernah courthouse that is a base for IS religious police, but missed and hit a house, killing at least 5 civilians.
The Shura Council of Darna's Jihadis attacked IS in response to the killing of their ledaer, Nasser Akr, by masked gunmen; 9 IS fighters and 2 jihadi fighters were killed in the fighting.
An armed militia entered the Tunisian consulate and abducted 10 staff members; the militia freed 3 captives after 5 days and the rest after one week.
notes: An ex-hostage stated that the kidnapping was in retaliation for the arrest of a Fajr Libya militia leader at the Tunis airport the previous month; he was freed on the same day the hostages were returned.

issuenote: Dozens of IS fighters were killed in fighting over the course of a week as the Mujahedeen Council of Derna launched an offensive to remove IS from Derna.

The US military carried out an air strike on a farm south of Ajdabiya and killed at least 17 militants; the strike targeted Al-Mourabitoun leader Mokhtar Balmokhtar, who was presumed dead and led to fighting near the Ajdabiya hospital betweeen the group that was injured and the Libyan military.
notes: The Pentagon announced the strike was believed successful, but had not confirmed Belmokhtar's death; AQIM denied his death several days later. Jihadist leader Seifallah Ben Hassine was later confirmed dead in the strike.

At least 10 civilians were killed and at least 15 were wounded when three separate car bombs exploded in Derna; the bombs set off clashes between IS fighters and al-Qaida-linked militias that continued into the next day.

issuenote: Taher Allush, a senior military intelligence officer algined with Fajr Libya, was killed in Misrata when a bomb hidden in his car exploded.

issuenote: Four Italian construction workers were kidnapped near the ENI oil complex in the Mellitah region; five days later they had not been found and the identity of the kidnappers was unknown.

IS claimed responsibility for a car bomb that exploded in Derna, killing 9 people and wounding dozens.

After IS assassinated an iman in Sirte, Fajr Libya called for an offensive to take back the city from IS; the result was five days of fighting between IS and local militants and Fajr Libya forces, which carried out air strikes; dozens were killed.

In the wake of more migrant deaths in the Mediterranean, protesters marched in Zuara to call for people not to rent homes to migrant smugglers, who use the homes to house migrants as they wait for the seas to be safe enough to cross.
IS and pro-government fighters clashed in Benghazi over two days; 5 loyalist fighters were killed.
A car bomb exploded outside the Eni offices in Tripoli, wounding 1 and damaging some buildings; no group claimed responsilbility.
IS fighters attacked an army position 8km south of Benghazi, killing at least 3 soldiers; the army responded by chasing the attackers, capturing some weapons and causing some casualties.
A car bomb exploded outside the Al-Habda al-Khadra prison in Tripoli, which destroyed 2 cars but caused no casualties.
Fajr Libya organized protests in Tripoli to encourage the Tripoli parliament to reject the recent draft of the peace accord.

issuenote: IS attacked the prison at the Mitiga airbase in Tripoli in an attempt to free Muslim detainees; at least 4 fighters and three people in the prison were killed.

A mortar round fired by Islamist militia killed four children playing soccer and an elderly man; it was suspected that the shell was fired to honor the recent killing of a senior Islamist fighter.
Hundreds gathered in  Benghazi to protest a proposed power-sharing and peace deal put forward by the UN; Islamists fired rockets on the protesters, killing 12 and wounding 39.
notes: Officials stated that it was the second deadly attack on a rally in Benghazi in one week.

notes: As of December 18, the two hostages were alive, but the Serbian government had received no demands for their release.

notes: The number of gunmen involved in the incident is not mentioned, and their identity and intentions were not known at the time of publication. The dead included two wounded members of the security forces and an ambulance medic.

issuenote: Gunmen opened fire on security forces, but were repulsed with casualties
notes: The total number of participants in not mentioned, no group has claimed responsibility for the attack, and the identities and motivation of the gunmen is not known. However, 5 "terrorists" were killed during the attack.

issuenote: A roadside bomb struck an armoured police vehicle.
notes: Although the total number of participants in the event is not mentioned, two policemen were killed in the attack. The identity and motivation of the attackers is not mentioned.

actor2: Sherif Ali, taxi driver and protest organizer
issuenote: Taxi drivers blocked a roundabout to demand that Uber be banned in Cairo.
notes: The number of taxi drivers involved in the protest is not mentioned. After a traffic jam began to build behind the protest, police fire tear gas at the drivers to disperse them.

issuenote: A soldier was killed by a bomb
notes: The total number of participants in the incident is not mentioned; nor is the identity and intentions of the perpetrators.

issuenote: Suspected militants launched mortar shells at an army camp
notes: The total number of participants in this incident is not mentioned, although 5 soldiers were killed in the attack and 10 wounded. Egyptian officials told AP that they attribute the attack to suspected ISIS militants operating in the region, though their basis for their decision is not mentioned.

issuenote: Militants attacked a police checkpoint
notes: The total number of participants in this incident is not mentioned, though 15 policemen were killed as well as 5 attackers. There is some dispute over the type of attack; the Egyptian government claims it was a mortar attacker while the ISIS affiliate says it was a suicide bombing accompanied by a raid by its fighters. In its statement, the ISIS affiliate claims the attack was revenge for "insults to Muslim women at checkpoints".

target1: Suspected gang members accused of involvement in the Guilo Regeni murder
issuenote: Police killed suspected gang members accused of being behind the kidnapping, torture and murder of an Italian graduate student.
notes: The number of police who participated in the shootout with the gang is not mentioned, though all five suspected gang members were killed and witnesses claimed seven squad cars surrounded the gang's car. According to police, this gang specializes in posing as police in order to kidnap and rob foreigners. Police say they recovered some of Regeni's belongings in the house of one of the gang members, and found fake police IDs, weapons, and electronic prod, and a body in the trunk of the gang's car. Regeni's parents reject this claim by the Egyptian government, saying that, except for his passport and student ID, the rest of the belongings the police found in the home they raided did not belong to their son. Many in Italy believe that Regeni's kidnapping and murder was perpetrated by Egyptian security forces. Witnesses claim the men were unarmed when they were gunned down by police, and relatives of the alleged gang members say they were housepainters who were killed by police while driving to a job, and were unconnected to the Regeni murders.

issuenote: Counterterrorism troops backed by air support attacked suspected militants
notes: The total number of participants in this incident is unknown. The military claims they "killed 60 terrorists, wounded another 40 and destroyed 27 four-wheel pick-up trucks", though AFP could not independently verify these figures.

issuenote: A man hijacked a domestic flight from Alexandria to Cairo.
notes: 72 people were aboard the aircraft. Mustafa's actions appear to have been the result of a dispute with his ex-wife, who is Cypriot. The plane was eventually diverted to Lanarca, Cyprus where Mustafa surrendered himself to police after a six-hour standoff which was characterized as "bizarre".

target1: Nadeem Centre for the Rehabilitation of Victims of Violence
issuenote: Officials attempted for the second time to close an NGO which provides medical treatment to alleged torture victims.
notes: The total number of participants in this incident is not mentioned.

actor1: Demonstrators opposed to Saudi-Egyptian territorial deal
actor2: University students protesting over Saudi-Egyptian territorial deal
issuenote: Protests broke out in two cities after Egypt signed an agreement to cede two islands to Saudi Arabia
notes: Both demonstrations were described as small, with about two dozen taking part in the Cairo protest and an unknown number taking part in the Damanhur protest. Police arrested five demonstrators in Cairo, and two protesting students in Damanhur. In addition to the protests, the transfers of these two islands from Egypt to Saudi Arabia prompted a storm of criticism on social media. The two islands, Tiran and Sanafir, are uninhabited and have been in Egypt's "protective custody" since 1950.

actor2: Secular activists dissatisfied with the government
issuenote: Protestors demonstrated against the government.

In Cairo, police dispersed protestors with tear gas and chased them through the streets, arresting an unspecified number of protestors. According to AFP, at least 2,000 protesters attended on demonstration among many in Cairo, leading them to estimate that thousands took part in the rallies in the three cities; AP counted around 200 protesters at the same protest.

actor1: Residents of the New Cairo district
issuenote: Protests erupted against police after a policeman killed a local street vendor.
notes: AP reported that scores of resident participated in the protest, while AFP noted dozens of participants. Protestors chanted "police are thugs" and smashed a police car and an ambulance that tried to block the road after the protest had begun. Riot police sealed off the area and dispersed the crowd. This was the latest in a series of incidents in which perceived incidents of police brutality touched off public protests.

issuenote: A policeman on patrol shot and killed a vendor over the price of a cup and tea, as well as wounding two passers-by
notes: In response to these incidents, a large protest broke out in the neighborhood against the police. In November, Abdel-Razzek as sentenced to life imprisonment for killing the vendor.

issuenote: Unidentified assailants fired an rocket-propelled grenade at a police convoy
notes: The number of assailants and their identity or affiliation (if any) is unknown. This area is home to ISIS-affiliated militants who have attacked police and military convoys before, but at the time of publication they had not claimed credit for the attack. Three policemen were killed in the attack and eight were wounded.

issuenote: Police rounded-up activists who called for protests on April 25.
notes: Both AP & AFP indicated that dozens were arrested in the days leading up to the protest, with one group of lawyers claiming that 59 people were arrested in Cairo alone. Amnesty International quoted an Egyptian human rights group which claimed that nearly 250 were arrested in total, Human Rights Watch says the number at least 382, and AP noted that nearly 100 were arrested in the pre-dawn hours of April 25 in Cairo. Once NGO lawyer noted that the round-up was targeting activists both in Cairo and in the provinces. April 25 is a national holiday to commemorate the return of the Sinai to Egyptian control. The wave of arrests continued after the protest as well, with human rights lawyers estimating for AP that close to 1,300 activists were arrested in a three week period. 51 people were eventually given two-year prison sentences in connection with the planned protests, and 151 were given five-year sentences (47 of those five-year sentences were later overturned on appeal),  7 received eight-year sentences in June, and 10 received three-year sentences in July. 82 were acquitted on appeal in June. Many activists have called for protests against the government's policies, including its decision to cede two islands to Saudi Arabia.

issuenote: Opposition members protested the government, but were dispersed by police after the protestors threw rocks at them.
notes: About 50 protestors participated in the incident. Leading liberal and leftist dissidents had called for protests on April 25 to mark the anniversary of the return of the Sinai to Egypt. Police dispersed the protest with tear gas.

issuenote: A roadside bomb struck a police convoy, killing three policemen.
notes: The total number of participants is not mentioned. The identity and issues motivating the attack are not clear; according to AP, no group had claimed credit for the attack, though AFP notes that ISIS-affiliated militants are active in the area. Eight policemen were also wounded in the attack

issuenote: Two journalists staged a sit-in at the journalists' association office, and were arrested after police stormed the building.
notes: According to Badr, both his and el-Sakka's homes were raided by police the day before they began their protest. Badr runs a website which is opposed to  President el-Sisi, while el-Sakka had announced on Facebook before the sit-in that he intended to join a protest against Egypt's transfer of two Red Sea islands to Saudi Arabia. Police responded by storming the building and arresting the journalists, charging them with "incitement to protest", and "firearms, Molotov cocktails and inflammatory leaflets" were found during a search of their homes. The head of the association, Yahiya Kallash, said "This is the first time that police have stormed the headquarters of the association". Badr was released on bail on August 28.

actor1: Kamal Abbas, Center for Trade Unions and Workers' Services
issuenote: Workers gathered near the journalists' syndicate to commemorate International Workers' Day, but police forced them to move to another location
notes: 650 workers gathered at the journalists' syndicate, but there way was blocked by dozens of armed and plain-clothes policemen. Instead, a smaller group gathered at the Center for Trade Unions and Workers' Services to denounce the police's actions as a suppression of the freedom of assembly. Under the Mubarak regime, the syndicate building was one of the few places where opposition protests were allowed, and is often a rallying point for demonstrations.

issuenote: Journalists staged a sit-in to protest a police raid on their headquarters and the detention of two of their colleagues, and called for the Interior Minister to resign.
notes: AP notes that dozens of journalists participated in the sit-in, but also commented that the size of the protest was limited by a heavy police presence around the Journalist Syndicate's headquarters. Hundreds of uniformed and plainclothes police patrolled the area around the building, blocking off side-streets and severely restricting access to the area. By April 3 hundreds had gathered outside the headquarters to show their support, and in a general assembly meeting on April 4, the Syndicate voted to demand that the reporters be released, Interior Minister Magdy Abdel Ghaffar resign and President el-Sissi issue a formal apology, and threatened a strike if the demands were not met.

issuenote: Several dozen counterdemonstrators chanted pro-government songs and slogan and denounced members of the journalists' union
notes: AP notes that several dozen demonstrators gathered at either end of the street in front of the Journalist Syndicate headquarters, though a more specific estimate was not provided.

target1: Malek Adly, human rights lawyer and prominent opposition activist
issuenote: Police arrested a prominent opposition lawyer
notes: The number of police participating in this incident was not mentioned. According to police, Adly was charged with joining a "group aimed at annulling the constitution". Adly had earlier filed a suit against the government attempting to block a treaty which transfers control of two islands to Saudi Arabia, which has become a political lightning rod in Egypt. Adly was released from jail on August 28.

issuenote: ISIS gunmen sprayed a police van with automatic rifle fire.
notes: The incident was reported to have occurred overnight, though precisely which day it occurred on is not mentioned. Four assailants were involved in the attack, with killed a lieutenant and seven policemen in plain-clothes. According to statement released by the ISIS affiliate, the attack was in retaliation for "the pure women imprisoned" in Egypt.

target1: Ezzedine Khaled, member of the satirical comedy street group "Street Children"
issuenote: Police arrested a man whose group produces satirical videos mocking the government.
notes: The number of police involved in the incident is not mentioned. According to police and Khaled's lawyer, Khaled was arrested for "inciting protests and publishing a video that insulted state institutions". In Street Children's latest parody video before the arrest, they sang songs and acted out skits about the devaluation of the Egyptian pound, the transfer of two islands from Egypt to Saudi Arabia, and made fun of the police and President el-Sissi. Khaled was released on bail on May 9. On June 23, Human Rights Watch called for the release of Khaled and four other members of Street Children who were arrested at the same time.

target1: Mohammed Adel, Mohammed Dessouki, Mohammed Yahya and Mohammed Gabr, members of the satirical comedy street group "Street Children"
issuenote: Police arrested four members of comedy group who make videos making fun of the government.
notes: The number of police involved in the incident is not mentioned. The four are accused of "promoting ideas calling for terrorist acts by posting a video on social networks and YouTube," "incitement to take part in demonstrations disturbing the public order" and "inciting mobs to commit hostile actions against state institutions". A fifth member of group, Ezzedine Khaled, was arrested on charges of "inciting protests and publishing a video that insulted state institutions" on May 7, but was released on May on bail. On June 23, Human Rights Watch called for the release of the five arrested members of Street Children. On September 11, Yehya, al-Dessouki and Gabr were released on parole.

issuenote: Pilots carried out a go-slow protest to demand a raise.
notes: The number of pilots who participated in the go-slow is not mentioned, nor are the locations effected by the protest specifically given. Unlike a strike, these pilots did not leave their workplace, though they did carry out their work a slower, less-productive pace than is typical. Though the pilots were demanding an 80%, they eventually received a 22% raise in 2016 and  18% raise in 2017.

target1: Managers of a shipyard belonging to the Egyptian Navy
issuenote: Striking workers staged a sit-in at a shipyard that was broken up by security forces.
notes: The date given here is an estimate; the actual date of the strike and its length are not mentioned. The number of strikers and their demands were not mentioned. Security forces arrested 13 striking workers and engineers.

actor1: Guards at the  Misr Spinning and Weaving factory
target1: Kamal al-Fayoumi, labor activists and former Misr Spinning and Weaving employee
issuenote: Guards detained and questioned a labor agitator for five hours.
notes: The date provided is an estimate, as exact dates were not mentioned. The number of participants in the incident is not mentioned. The guards and security forces questioned al-Fayoumi about his labor activism and possible links to foreign sources of funding

target1: Mina Thabet, Director of the Minority and Religious Groups Department of the Egyptian Commission for Rights and Freedoms (an NGO)
issuenote: Police arrested a prominent advocate for Egyptian Coptic Christians
notes: The number of participants in this incident is not mentioned. Thabet faces a number of charges, including inciting terrorist activities via the internet and inciting protests. The head of the Egyptian Commission for Rights and Freedoms, Ahmed Abdullah, was also arrested by police in April. Thabet is well known for rights for the Egypt's Copts.

target2: Elderly Coptic Christian woman whose son allegedly had an affair with a Muslim women
issuenote: Rioting villagers burned the homes of Coptic Christian and paraded an elderly Coptic woman through the streets naked after they learned her son was having an affair with a Muslim woman.
notes: The number of rioters is not mentioned by either source, though AP indicates that police arrested 6 suspects in connection with the violence and were looking for 12 more. Sexual relations between members of different faiths are taboo in Egypt, particularly in rural Egypt and particularly between Christian men and Muslim women. Seven homes belonging to Copts were looted and burned during the riot. Although police eventually arrived to disperse the riot, a prominent Coptic cleric said the police had ignored earlier complaints by the Coptic woman's family of threats from the villagers, and failed to arrive to disperse the riot until two hours after it had begun.

target1: Hesham Genana, former head of the Central Auditing Organization
issuenote: Police summoned a former auditor for questioning and detained him for spreading "false news".
notes: The date given for this event is an estimate; the source indicates only that Genana was summoned for questioning in May. The number of participants in this incident is not mentioned. The charge results from a newspaper which quoted Genana as saying that corruption cost the country 600 billion Egyptian pounds in 2015; Genana maintains he was misquoted and that this figure in fact covered the previous four years.

issuenote: Police suffered a roadside bombing
notes: The number of participants in this incident is not mentioned. Two policemen were killed and three others were wounded by the bomb.

issuenote: Police arrested three leaders of Egypt's journalists union.
notes: The number of participants in this incident is not mentioned. Police charged the three men with harboring fugitives and publishing false news. On November 19, all three were convicted of "harboring fugitives" and sentenced to two years in jail each.

issuenote: A roadside bomb struck a military convoy, killing six soldiers.
notes: The number and affiliation of the bombers, as well as their goals, is not mentioned. In addition to the 6 soldiers killed in the attack, a further six were wounded.

notes: AP notes that approximately two dozen supporters gathered for the demonstration, while AFP puts the number at closer to 50. Scores of riot police, along with armoured vehicles, where also present, though they did not intervene.

issuenote: Four masked gunmen stormed as house and shot two policemen inside.
notes: The identity of the gunmen and their motive for launching this attack are not mentioned in the statement released by the Interior Ministry. However, AP notes that this attack bears the hallmarks of similar attacks by ISIS-affiliated militants.

issuenote: High school students protested a government decision requiring them to retake their final exams
notes: This date is an estimate; a specific date was not mentioned. The number of participants in this incident is not mentioned. The Egyptian government required students to retake their final exams after the answers to the exams were leaked on Facebook. Scores on these exams determine whether students will be accepted into state universities, and competition is fierce for spots in fields like engineering and medicine.

actor1: Demonstrators opposed to Saudi-Egyptian territorial deal
issuenote: Demonstrators cheered a decision by the Administrative Court of overturn a treaty with Saudi Arabia.
notes: AP notes that about two dozen demonstrators were present. The treaty in question would have ceded control of two islands (Tiran and Sanafir) to Saudi Arabia, and opposition to the treaty sparked numerous protests in April, 2016.

actor1: Demonstrators opposed to Saudi-Egyptian territorial deal
issuenote: Demonstrators protested outside a courthouse, and heckled government lawyers and tussled with and shouted at policemen inside.
notes: AP notes that dozens participated in the protest. The appeals court was hearing the government's case against a decision by the Administrative Court to overturn a territorial agreement with Saudi Arabia that has become a political lightning rod in Egypt.

issuenote: Troops engaged in a gun battle with smugglers attempting to cross the Egypt-Libya border.
notes: The number of soldiers participating in this incident is not mentioned. According to a statement released by military spokesman Brigadier General Mohammed Samir, 6 Egyptian soldiers were killed and 3 wounded in the clash, with an unspecified number of smugglers also killed.

issuenote: ISIS-affiliated gunmen gunned down a Coptic Christian priest standing next to his car.
notes: The number of participants in this incident is not mentioned. ISIS claimed credit for the attack, saying that a "squad" of gunmen killed the priest for "combating Islam".

issuenote: Suspected militants wounded a soldier with a bomb blast before attacking the ambulance carrying him to the hospital.
notes: Egyptian sources speaking with AP alleged that the bomb was planted by Islamist militants, though the number of participants is not mentioned.

issuenote: Suspected militants killed a policeman with a bomb outside the main city hospital
notes: Egyptian sources speaking with AP alleged that the bomb was planted by Islamist militants, though the number of participants is not mentioned. Two other policemen were also wounded in the attack.

issuenote: Two police officers were killed by a roadside bomb believed to have been planted by ISIS-affiliated militants
notes: The number of participants in this incident is not mentioned. Although Egypt's ISIS-affiliate claimed credit for the bombing of a police mine clearing vehicle, AFP stated it was unclear if this was the same attack referenced in the statement released by the Interior Ministry. Three others were wounded in addition to the two officers killed by the bomb.

issuenote: Muslim villagers attacked and burned down the homes of Coptic Christian villagers
notes: This date is an estimate; a specific date was not provided. The size of the mob was not mentioned. The attacks began after a rumor spread that a Christian was going to turn the kindergarten into a church. Whether police intervened to disperse the mob is not mentioned, although similar incidents have resulted in intervention by the police.

issuenote: Gunmen assassinated a local police chief
notes: The date provided is an estimate; only the month was mentioned but not the specific date. The number of participants in this incident is also not mentioned.

issuenote: Muslim villagers attacked and burned down the homes of Coptic Christian villagers
notes: The size of the mob was not mentioned. The attacks began after a rumor spread that a Christian was going to turn the kindergarten into a church. Police intervened and arrested at least 14 people.

target1: Families of two Coptic Christian priests
issuenote: A Muslim mob attacked the families of two Coptic Christian priests with batons and knives over a personal feud
notes: The size of the mob was not mentioned. One family member, Fam Khalaf, was stabbed to death by the mob, and the father of one of the priests was wounded during the attack. Police dispersed the mob and arrested four people.

target1: Muslim villagers responsible for the death of Fam Khalaf
issuenote: Mourners marched from a church to a graveyard to protest the murder of a family member of Coptic Christian priest
notes: The number of mourners is not mentioned. Khalaf had been stabbed to death the previous day by angry Muslim mob over a personal feud between the Muslims villagers and the families of two Coptic Christian priest. Khalaf was related to one of the priests.

issuenote: A gunman affiliated with ISIS shot and killed a policeman
notes: According to the Interior Ministry, only one gunman participated in the attack. Egypt's ISIS affiliate claimed credit for the attack, saying its fighters had assassinated the policemen and stolen his car and weapon.

target1: Abu Doaa al-Ansari, leader of Egypt's ISIS-affiliate

issuenote: Counterterrorism troops backed by air support killed an ISIS-affiliate leader, several of his aides and other militants.

The total number of deaths is not clear, as the number of aides killed in the attack is not mentioned. The details of the attack and the identity of al-Ansari could not be independently confirmed, as press access to Sinai is heavily restricted by the Egyptian military. In addition, the Egyptian military did not release al-Ansari's real name.

actor1: Gunmen belonging to the Hasm group
target1: Sheikh Ali Gomaa, former Grand Mufti of Egypt
issuenote: Two gunmen opened fire on the former Grand Mufti of Egypt as he walked to a mosque, though the mufti escaped unharmed.
notes: After the attack began, Gomaa's bodyguards returned fire, and police were searching for the perpetrators. Hasm claims it launched the attack to resist the "military occupation of Egypt by militias of (President) Abdel-Fatah el-Sissi", and provided pictures of the gunmen. It is not known whether Hasm is affiliated with any other groups. Gomaa was Grand Mufti until 2013, and supported el-Sissi's overthrow of the Islamist Morsi government.

issuenote: Coptic Christians demonstrated to demand their rights be upheld in interfaith disputes.
notes: AP notes that three dozen Copts protested, but did not provide a more specific estimate. The source also notes that an equal number of police set up roadblocks and forced the demonstrators to disperse after an hour.

issuenote: Three gunmen in a car opened fire on a police checkpoint
notes: At the time of the attack, he identities of the three gunmen, their motives, and whether they were affiliated with an group was not mentioned, and the Interior Ministry said it was investigating the attack. Subsequently the group Liwa al-Thawra claimed credit for the attack, though the veracity of their claim could not be verified and their motive for the attack was not mentioned. Two policemen were killed during the attack, and one policeman and two civilians were wounded. A latter report by AP claimed that three policemen were wounded in the attack

issuenote: An assailant stabbed a guard at a Coptic church, before being killed by other guards.
notes: The identity of the attacker and his motive were not known at the time the story was released. Whether the guard who was stabbed died of his wounds is not clear; as a result, only the death of the attacker is recorded here.

issuenote: Mothers protested the shortage of subsidized baby formula
notes: AP reports that scores of women participated in the protest, but the exact number of participants is not provided.

target1: Hamdy Mokhtar, Mohammed Hassan, and Osama al-Bishbishi, all journalists conducting street interviews
issuenote: Police arrested three journalists conducting street interviews and one interviewing protestors
notes: The number of participants in this incident is not mentioned. Mokhtar, Hassan and al-Bishbishi were arrested on September 26, Nasser on September 27. All four were charged with publishing false news, and Mokhtar, Hassan and al-Bishbishi were also charged with belonging to banned organization (which in Egypt is typically shorthand for the Muslim Brotherhood). Mokhtar, Hassan and al-Bishbish were interview passers-by on the street about President el-Sissi's proposal to allow Egyptians to donate fractions of checks they cash to the government.

issuenote: Three unidentified assailants intercepted a taxi carrying three policemen and killed all the occupants.
notes: The participant's affiliation and motive is not mentioned, though similar attacks have been launched by Egypt's ISIS affiliate, which operates in the region. The three policemen were killed on site, and the driver died of his wounds at the hospital.

target1: Zakareya Abdel Aziz, deputy prosecutor general
issuenote: A car bomb exploded as the deputy prosecutor general drove past.
notes: The number of participants in this incident was not mentioned. Hasm claimed credit for the attack and threatened further attacks against the "oppressive judiciary". Abdel Aziz and his bodyguards were not harmed in the attack, though a passing bystander was wounded.

issuenote: ISIS-affiliated militants attacked security forces constructing a checkpoint, but were repulsed with casualties.
notes: The number of participants in this incident is not mentioned. According to Egyptian authorities, the attack was carried out by ISIS-affiliated militants looking to disrupt construction of the checkpoint. All five deaths were on the militant side, with no reports of casualties on government side.

issuenote: Suspected ISIS-affiliated militants kidnapped four Sufi clerics.
notes: The number of participants in this incident is not mentioned. The four clerics had a history of speaking out against the killing of local civilians by ISIS-affiliated militants, and Egyptian officials attributed the attack to these militants.

issuenote: Suspected ISIS-affiliated militants ambushed a taxi carrying off-duty policemen and sprayed it with gunfire.
notes: The number of participants in this incident is not mentioned. The policemen were returning to their duty stations when the ambush occurred. A specific location was not provided. Egyptian officials attributed the attack to these militants

issuenote: Suspected ISIS-affiliated militants attacked a police armoured personal carrier with a roadside bomb.
notes: The number of participants and the exact location of the incident is not mentioned. The attacked initially wounded nine policemen, with one of the wounded subsequently dying of their wounds at the hospital. Egyptian officials attributed the attack to these militants

target1: Employees of the state electric company
issuenote: A car carrying four workers at state-owned industry hit a roadside bomb.
notes: The number of participants in this incident is not mentioned. Three workers were killed instantly by the attack, while the other worker died of his wounds at the hospital. Egyptian officials attributed the attack to these militants

target1: Dr. Mohammed Kamal, senior Muslim Brotherhood leader
target2: Shahata Ali Ragab, Muslim Brotherhood member
issuenote: A senior Muslim Brotherhood leader and another member were killed in a shoot-out with police.
notes: The number of participants in this incident is not mentioned. There is some dispute over how Dr. Kamal and Ragab died; police say they were shot in a firefight while the Muslim Brotherhood announced that they had been arrested and killed while in custody. Dr. Kamal had been sentenced twice in absentia to life in prison for founding an armed group and for his involvement in a police station bombing in Assiut. According to police, he was also suspected of involvement in dozens of attacks, including the murder of Egypt's chief prosecutor in 2015 and a 2016 assassination attempt on former Grand Mufti Sheikh Ali Gomaa.

issuenote: ISIS-affiliated militants fired mortars and rockets at an army checkpoint before attacking it with all terrain vehicles and small arms
notes: The number of participants in this incident is not mentioned. Twelve Egyptian soldiers were killed and six wounded during the attack. issuenote: Militants surronded a mosque, detonated a bomb outside the mosque, blocked escape routes with burning vehciles, and gunned down civilans and soldiers in the mosque with small arms fire and rocket-propelled greandes as they attempted to flee, killing 305 people and wounding 129 people.
notes: After the attack, the Egyptian Air Force launched on locations that it claims were used by terrorists to store munitions, and claimed to have destroyed several vehicles used by the militants during the attack, killing the occupants. Although ISIS did not claim credit for the attack, AP and AFP note that a ISIS-affiliated militants in Egypt have conducted numerous attacks in the Sinai Peninsula against soldiers, civilians alleged to be collaborating with the government, and Sufis. AFP notes that while the mosque is associated with a Sufi order, both Sufi and non-Sufi were present during the attack.
